title: Eidolon Shard: The Great Labyrinth of Egypt
premise: At a fictionalized labyrinth inspired by Egyptian myth and prior game-map work, the player crosses a symbolic surface plan and a mirrored basement while a 12-hour cycle repeats. Four reconciled fragments open the central rosette and the shaft below; twelve courts ultimately align a symbolic Solar Barque.
truth_boundary: This is a game-design interpretation, not an archaeological claim. Historical details should be distinguished from mythic, symbolic, speculative, and invented elements.
principles: Puzzles should have physical or symbolic causality rather than arbitrary locks.
The time loop preserves player memory while most world systems partially reset.
Failure changes information and relationships instead of merely blocking progress.

simulation_profile.time_model: semi-Markov 12-hour loop with persistent divergence flags
simulation_profile.physics_resolution: local architectural acoustics, light transport cues, thermal inertia, observer uncertainty
simulation_profile.randomness_policy: seeded PCG32; hidden layout facts sampled once; action uncertainty sampled per attempt

player_setup.starting_familiar: Ba, a celestial falcon-like memory companion

map_layers.role: ritual clue layer and upper maze

loop_rules: At the end of Hour 12, transient doors, NPC positions, and unsolved court events reset.
Player memory, ledger, fused glyphs, earned trust, and explicit divergence flags persist.
A solved court may repeat with altered context rather than vanishing from play.

sensory_model.light: oil flame, reflected sunlight, starlight shafts, mineral fluorescence only when fiction establishes a source
sensory_model.sound: long stone reverberation, occluded corridors, footstep delay, air-shaft resonance
sensory_model.temperature: slow stone thermal response with cooler lower passages
sensory_model.perception: uncertainty rises in darkness, echoic spaces, fatigue, and unfamiliar symbolic contexts

factions.goal: break the loop regardless of collateral consequences

factions.name: Scribes of the Returning Word
factions.goal: record every divergence and test whether memory changes destiny

characters.name: Neseret
characters.role: keeper of the eastern mirror court

locations.name: South Processional Start
hooks: wind-driven sand traces a repeating geometry

quests.title: Reconcile the Four Corners
quests.goal: recover and interpret star, solar, scarab, and serpent fragments

quests.title: The Mirror Does Not Agree
quests.goal: solve paired basement rooms whose observations differ
quests.completion: derive the invariant shared by both rooms

quests.title: The Twelve Courts
quests.goal: cause a meaningful divergence in each hour/court

quests.title: What Deserves to Persist?
quests.goal: decide which memories the loop should preserve for everyone, not only the player
quests.completion: constitutional memory rule authored by player

clocks.on_max: route closure and new detour, not instant death

encounters.dilemma: follow a voice whose delay does not match the corridor geometry
east and west chambers provide individually consistent but mutually incompatible inscriptions
a Keeper offers a shortcut in exchange for surrendering one remembered clue
activation can end the loop but may erase stable identities that formed inside it

mechanics.core_resolution: logistic skill-vs-difficulty probability with contextual modifiers and seeded replay
mechanics.loop_divergence: persistent flags survive resets; transient physical state does not unless causally stabilized
mechanics.glyph_fusion: combine discovered symbolic constraints; valid fusion must explain at least two prior observations
mechanics.acoustic_puzzles: use distance, sound speed, reverb, and occlusion as clue generators
mechanics.light_puzzles: use source direction, reflection, occlusion, spectrum, and time-of-day as clue generators
mechanics.failure: reveal cost, altered route, trust change, or new information; avoid dead-end rerolls

memory_rules.rewind: allowed only by explicit player command; mark ledger branch

image_direction.style: cinematic archaeological-fantasy realism; monumental scale; physically plausible light; no pseudo-hieroglyphic gibberish in close-up
image_direction.camera: 24–50 mm equivalent; strong architectural perspective; viewpoint-height continuity
image_direction.continuity: preserve character clothing, injuries, carried objects, room geometry, and light sources across turns

llm_directives: Open on sensory evidence, not lore exposition.
Treat Egyptian religion and history respectfully; label invented or speculative material when relevant out of character.
Never make a hidden solution true merely because the player guessed it; consult stable world state.
Use the physics layer to generate clues, not to bury the player in equations.
When the player proposes an experiment, simulate what the experiment could actually reveal.
Offer freeform actions in addition to listed options.

endings.name: Solar Release
endings.condition: 12 glyphs aligned and informed consent rule satisfied

endings.name: Commonwealth of Memory
endings.condition: player reforms loop so inhabitants share bounded persistent memory

endings.name: The Door Remains Open
endings.condition: player rejects a final answer and converts the labyrinth into an ongoing school of inquiry

research_notes: Prior project map: symbolic surface, rectilinear basement, 64-node playable abstraction, central rosette to central shaft.
Prior Eidolon Shard concept: 12-hour cycle, 12 courts/Nomoi, glyph fusion, Ba familiar, Solar Barque.
Historical/mythic details in this mod must be treated as inspiration, not asserted archaeology.
